question: Should we judge others?
summary: Jesus in Matthew 7:1 and Luke 6:37 commands his followers not to judge, and Paul echoes that in Romans 2:1 and 14:10 along with James 4:12. But Leviticus 19:15 commands righteous judgment of one's neighbor, John 7:24 has Jesus telling people to "judge righteous judgment," and Paul in 1 Corinthians 5-6 demands the Corinthians judge an immoral brother and even angels.

reconcile.connective: Commentators harmonize by distinguishing senses of "judge": the prohibition targets censorious, hypocritical, private condemnation, while civil and corrective righteous judgment remains commanded.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells, who catalogs this in the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, presses that the texts issue flatly opposing commandments on whether believers should judge others at all.

pd_work.note: Henry treats this passage directly, harmonizing it by distinguishing the magistrate's/minister's office of judging from the private, censorious judging Christ prohibits.

link.title: GotQuestions: What does the Bible mean when it says, "Do not judge"?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment reconciling Matthew 7:1 with the call to righteous judgment (John 7:24; 1 Corinthians).

excerpts.excerpt_text: He speaketh not here of civil judgments, and therefore by the word, forgive, is meant that good nature, which the Christians use in suffering and pardoning wrongs.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the tension by restricting Christ's "judge not" to a sense other than civil/legal judging, which Lev 19:15 and 1 Cor command.
